title: Getting around faster
text:
GETTING AROUND FASTER
Training notes, E. Hale.
F brings the camera to what is selected; double-click a name in the Hierarchy does the same.
Shift with W A S D flies three times faster. Settings > Camera changes the speed.
Ctrl + drag in the 3D view selects several objects; they move together.
The search box of the Hierarchy finds any object of the map by name or class.
Every shortcut can be changed in Settings > Keyboard shortcuts. Mine are still the defaults. I am a creature of habit.

title: Building rooms
text:
BUILDING ROOMS
Training notes, E. Hale.
+ Block makes walls, floors and platforms; R stretches them.
+ Hole cuts a doorway in a wall or a pit in a floor.
Pieces (bottom bar) are ready-made parts of the game's own levels: a staircase, a desk corner, a whole office.
Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V copy objects and structures, even from one map to another.
Check map lists what is wrong before you play: links to nothing, objects inside walls, exits to no map.
Run it every time. Engineering still remembers my corridor that led nowhere.

title: Interactions, pro tips
text:
INTERACTIONS: PRO TIPS
Training notes, E. Hale.
A rule can do several things, each after its own seconds: a door opens, two seconds later the lights go out.
Once makes a rule fire only the first time.
A collision box (Objects > Triggers) is the way to say: when JC enters this area.
Map > Logic lists every rule of the map as a sentence: the place to look when something does not happen.
A rule can also play a cutscene.
The lights going out two seconds after the door is the oldest trick in this facility. It still works on recruits.

title: Characters and animation
text:
CHARACTERS AND ANIMATION
Training notes, E. Hale.
Tools > Character Creator makes new characters from the faces, bodies and clothes of the game. Dr. Hale was made that way. He chose the glasses himself.
Orders, faction, what a character carries: all in its Properties.
Draw route makes a patrol: click the points, the character walks them.
For a real wave, make one in the Animation Studio, or import a Mixamo animation (Waving, saved as FBX) and save it: it becomes a When idle animation like the others.

title: Story and flags
text:
STORY AND FLAGS
Training notes, E. Hale.
A dialogue can branch: JC's answers lead to different lines, and an answer can set a flag.
Flags are the story's memory: Only if a flag is set, a dialogue or an event waits for it. Like this facility, a good story never forgets who did what.
The person button next to a flag picks what happened to a character: killed, knocked out, alive.
InfoLinks are one-way: only the caller speaks.
When something does not start, the game's log explains it: Revision/System/Revision.log, the lines that start with UCEd.

title: Sharing your map
text:
SHARING YOUR MAP
Read this one twice. Legal reads it three times.
A map built from scratch is yours: it uses the game's textures and objects by name, from the player's own install.
A changed original map, or one with pieces of the game's levels, belongs partly to the game: share only your changes, never the map itself.
Install puts your maps in Revision/DeusEdixMaps; uninstalling DeusEdix takes that folder out of Revision.ini again.
DeusEdix is a fan-made tool, not affiliated with the Revision team, Eidos or Square Enix.
